title: Rappolo's tone and playing with Brunis in Ted Lewis' band
summary: He praises Rappolo and Brunis' tailgate trombone, then says they played together again in Ted Lewis' band from 1929.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, he really did impress me. He was so far ahead of his time, he wasn't even funny. It was amazing what a tone he...
On the record, even, you can tell the beautiful tone. I just wondered how he was in person. I never heard him.

Oh, yes. The symphony, Chicago Symphony, used to come down and just marvel at him. How he could... Couldn't read a note and get this wonderful tone and execution. Of course, it was Georgie Brunus. No one could beat him as far as tailgate trombone.
Anything else you can tell while we're thinking about George? Have you seen him lately? I haven't...
I haven't seen George in two, three years. He's working in Chicago. Yeah, I know he's still up there.

We want to get back to the New Orleans fellas in a minute, too, if we have time. But tell us a little bit about when you played with George after. You mentioned that first band. Then when was the next time that you played with him?
When I joined Ted Lewis in 1929. 1929.
How long did you stay with Ted Lewis and how long was George with you at that time?
Well, George was with Ted Lewis about 16 years and I was with him about seven.
Was George there all the time you were there? Yes. Because all the records that you were on, George would be on then, too?
Well, now there's some records that George, he didn't make. He left the band. Temporarily.
